title: Frontend-service route fallback gated by grafana.mtFallback allow list
answers: Why does a route show a loading/progress screen instead of the page for a while?
How do I add a route to the MT instant-startup allow list?
Where is the fallback loader for unsupported routes implemented?
Why does my new route briefly render PageFallbackLoader instead of my component?
body: Symptom: navigating to certain routes under the frontend-service split briefly shows a generic progress/skeleton screen (PageFallbackLoader) for up to 60s instead of the real page, even though the route works. Root cause/mechanism: GrafanaRoute calls useMTFallback(location) which reads the grafana.mtFallback feature flag value ({ allowList: string[] }) and matches location.pathname against each pattern with react-router-dom-v5-compat's matchPath; if the path isn't matched by any allow-list entry, it's treated as unsupported and the fallback renders until a 60s timeout elapses or the flag/path changes. Fix pattern: to make a route skip the fallback, add its path (or a wildcard like '/dashboards/*' to cover nested routes) to the allowList value of the grafana.mtFallback flag — don't special-case it in GrafanaRoute. Constraints: an empty/missing allowList means every route is allowed (no fallback shown); wildcard matching relies on matchPath semantics, so patterns must be valid route-path syntax, not glob.
applies: Any route rendered via GrafanaRoute in the frontend-service (MT instant startup) architecture.
